blocks.text: Krishna Defence & Allied Industries (KDAIL) is a small Gujarat-based metallurgy and fabrication business. It hot-rolls naval-grade steel plate into 'bulb bar' hull stiffeners for warships, and also makes special-alloy welding wire and electrodes, low-magnetic ballast bricks for submarines, armoured steel profiles for T-90 tank chassis and a high-altitude space heater for the Army [F] (CALL May 2026; AR2026 p.9). It earns money by winning purchase orders from Navy-approved shipyards and defence factories. Delivery runs on 6-12 month cycles, and revenue is recognised at a point in time when goods are delivered [F] (CALL Nov 2025; AR2026 p.123). A legacy stainless-steel dairy and kitchen equipment line runs from a separate plant at Kalol [F] (AR2026 p.8).

subsections.title: Listing status and what it means for the evidence base

blocks.text: KDAIL listed on the NSE Emerge SME platform in 2022 and moved to the NSE main board on 30 December 2025 [F] (AR2026 p.20; AR2026 p.36). It is not listed on BSE: the only exchange named is NSE [F] (AR2026 p.64), even though management said in May 2025 that it was applying to both NSE and BSE [MC] (CALL May 2025). As an SME-listed company it did not have to publish quarterly results until December 2025 [F] (AR2026 p.62). FY26 is its first Ind AS annual report, with a transition date of 1 April 2024 [F] (AR2026 p.88). Our statements data has only four annual columns (FY23-FY26) [F] (NUMBERS).

The audited record of the current business is short. There are two years of Ind AS accounts and four years of annual data in total. Quarterly data before December 2025 was not filed with the exchange in the normal course, and no Q1 FY27 earnings-call transcript was available to us, only the investor presentation. No prospectus was available. [F] (AR2026 p.62; NUMBERS)

subsections.title: Bear thesis: the strongest reasons not to own it

items: 1. Order book shrinking, and the opening figure was revised. Management reported a year-end FY25 order book of Rs 270 cr ('INR 2,700 million') [MC] (CALL May 2025). A year later the MD said the April 2025 opening was Rs 190 cr [MC] (CALL May 2026). The order book stood at Rs 103 cr at March 2026 and Rs 117 cr at June 2026 [F] (AR2026 p.10; PPT Aug 2026). These figures are not reconciled.

2. H2 FY26 order inflow guidance appears missed. Management guided Rs 100-150 cr of H2 inflow [MC] (CALL Nov 2025). The roll-forward from Rs 196 cr (Sep-25) to Rs 103 cr (Mar-26) on ~Rs 124 cr of H2 revenue implies ~Rs 32 cr of inflow [E] (CALL Nov 2025; AR2026 p.10).

3. Valuation has detached from every scenario in our DCF model. Price is Rs 1,001 against bear/base/bull values of Rs 96.6/200.8/302.5. The reverse DCF requires ~78% sales CAGR for five years, against 17.8% in the base case [F] (NUMBERS).

4. FY26 cash flow was flattered by a one-off. Inventory fell from Rs 72.4 cr to Rs 16.3 cr, releasing Rs 56.1 cr of the Rs 86.0 cr CFO, and raw-material purchases halved to Rs 67.3 cr [F] (AR2026 p.84; AR2026 p.114). CFO had been negative in FY23-FY25 [F] (NUMBERS).
5. Customer concentration is high and rising. Three customers took 60.8% of FY26 revenue, up from 56.6% in FY25 [E] (AR2026 p.123). The largest single customer is ~30-35% [MC] (CALL May 2026).

6. Execution penalties are large. The late-delivery (LD) provision created in FY26 was Rs 14.9 cr, ~6.1% of revenue, against Rs 5.3 cr in FY25 [E] (AR2026 p.143). This sits awkwardly with the rating agency's 'timely execution' language [F] (RATING).
7. Top-line momentum has stalled. Q1 FY27 revenue fell 14.7% year on year and TTM sales of Rs 234 cr are below FY26's Rs 245 cr [F] (NUMBERS).

8. Disclosure is inconsistent. The annual report contains three different FY25 revenue figures (Rs 189.6 / 194.9 / 202.0 cr) [F] (AR2026 p.82; AR2026 p.113; AR2026 p.123). Capacity claims range from 'up to Rs 200 cr' to Rs 400-500 cr [MC] (CALL Nov 2025; CALL May 2026). The governance report misdescribes the board and audit committee [F] (AR2026 p.58; AR2026 p.60).

9. Related-party and remuneration drift. Land and buildings were bought from a promoter company (Rs 4.67 cr) and flats from the MD [F] (AR2026 p.125). Shareholders are asked to approve MD pay of up to Rs 17.5 lakh a month, against Rs 10 lakh, plus 1% profit commission for non-executive directors [F] (AR2026 p.233; AR2026 p.237).

10. The new ventures are pre-revenue and consume management attention. The AUV, smart ammunition, composites and arresting gear are all developmental [MC] (CALL May 2026). A ~Rs 10 cr composites revenue target for FY26 was missed [MC] (CALL Nov 2024; CALL May 2026).

blocks.text: [AI] The market appears to price KDAIL as a scalable defence-platform story. The evidence describes something narrower: a competent, approval-protected supplier of a few naval steel products. It has a thin and shrinking order book, high shipyard concentration, a single year of positive operating cash flow, and a profit base inflated by an unusual working-capital release. Our variant view runs both ways. Margins may be more durable than a sceptic assumes, because job work has moved in-house and Q1 FY27 printed 26.3%. But the revenue line is less visible than the 30%+ guidance implies, and the share price requires growth (78% CAGR in the reverse DCF) that no disclosed order, capacity or pipeline figure supports [F] (NUMBERS; PPT Aug 2026).

items: 1. Order: the Navy or Coast Guard places a ship order on a shipyard. KDAIL receives a purchase order for hull steel within about a month, through limited tenders [MC] (CALL Nov 2025; CALL Nov 2024).

5. Inspection: Navy inspection before dispatch to the shipyard; NABL-accredited in-house labs [MC] (CALL Nov 2024; AR2026 p.12).
6. Delivery and billing: deliveries run 5-12 months; defence customers get ~30 days' credit [MC] (CALL Nov 2025; RATING). Delivery delays attract liquidated damages [F] (AR2026 p.143).

subsections.title: Where value is captured, and capital intensity

blocks.text: [AI] Value is captured at qualification and conversion, not at raw material. The steel plate is bought from the same approved mills any qualified rival would use. KDAIL's margin rests on holding one of reportedly two approvals [MC] (CALL Nov 2025) and on rolling and heat-treatment yields. Management says yield gains on larger batches drove FY26 margins [MC] (CALL Nov 2025).

The business is asset-light by design. Net block was Rs 34 cr against Rs 245 cr of sales in FY26, a fixed-asset turnover of 7.2x [F] (NUMBERS), and management describes itself as 'always asset light' [MC] (CALL Nov 2025). [AI] The capital that matters is working capital: inventory days were 270 in FY25 before falling to 47 in FY26 [F] (NUMBERS), together with performance bank guarantees of Rs 31.65 cr [F] (AR2026 p.117).

subsections.title: Export strategy, currency and trade policy

blocks.text: Exports are negligible: foreign-exchange earnings were Rs 3.05 lakh and outgo was nil in FY26 [F] (AR2026 p.42). Naval-grade bulb bars and weld consumables are classified and cannot be exported [MC] (CALL May 2026). Export upside is limited to commercial grades and to composite doors in Southeast Asia and the Middle East via the VABO JV [MC] (CALL May 2025). [AI] Currency exposure is minimal on both revenue and inputs, since CIF value of imported inputs was nil [F] (AR2026 p.42). No tariff or trade-policy exposure is disclosed beyond macro commentary on US reciprocal tariffs [F] (AR2026 p.32). The MD dismissed reciprocal procurement opening as irrelevant to naval steel [MC] (CALL May 2025).

Single-location risk: all defence manufacturing sits at Halol, Gujarat [F] (AR2026 p.8), and the Halol property is pledged to Axis Bank [F] (AR2026 p.110). Any disruption at that site would hit roughly 90% of revenue [AI].

subsections.title: Naval hull steel (bulb bars and weld consumables): the core

blocks.text: Position in the value chain: KDAIL is a tier-2 materials supplier to tier-1 shipyards. It sits between steel mills (SAIL, AMNS) and the hull fabricator [MC] (CALL Nov 2024). What exists today: 4,000-4,500 t of bulb-bar capacity and roughly 60% utilisation [MC] (CALL May 2026; CALL Nov 2025). Bulb bars plus weld consumables were ~75% of FY26 revenue [MC] (CALL May 2026), or ~Rs 184 cr [E]. Government exposure: effectively 100% of this line is state shipyards or the Navy [AI]. Bulb bars are 10-15% of ship weight [MC] (CALL Nov 2025) and are consumed in the first two years of a build [MC] (CALL Nov 2025).

blocks.text: [AI] Strategic implication: if the 3,000-5,000 t market estimate is anywhere near right, KDAIL's expanded capacity already approaches the whole naval market. Growth would then have to come from commercial grades, new profiles and share gains against the one rival, not from volume alone. This is the single most important unverified number in the thesis.

Today KDAIL supplies 26 profiles to HVF Avadi for T-90 chassis [MC] (CALL May 2026), about 15% of FY26 revenue [MC] (CALL May 2026), or ~Rs 37 cr [E]. Management claims sole-supplier status [MC] (CALL Nov 2024) and expects 20-30% growth [MC] (CALL Nov 2025). [AI] This is the most credible diversification away from shipyards, but it is tied to a single legacy tank platform whose production horizon is not disclosed.
